schoolReviews.review: My daughter is in Kindergarten here. Her teacher speaks to all of the parents every morning and has great communication with the families. I always know how my daughter is doing and how her day went. She loves classes like garden science and is learning her numbers and letters quickly. There is no shortage of parent volunteers for this class. We feel really fortunate to be in this school district and in Mrs. Smith’s Kindergarten class at Lafayette.

Small school community with highly involved PTA. Great garden program and enrichment opportunities. There are many wonderfully talented teachers. This has become mired by the poor leadership and permissiveness that gives some groups more power and influence over the direction of the school leading to discrimination against students and families.
Lafayette is served by incredible, caring teachers, wonderful staff and an awesome team of parents, who are highly involved. We love it's small, community feel!

A principal who is part of the problem. Defensive and ignorant of her shortcomings. We are leaving the school because of it. In our four years there, 2 teachers have been amazing and 2 have been absolutley horrible. Racism and bullying has been pushed aside and not handled well at all. We are leaving because we are not safe or supported by the principal.

11 out of 10. Before our first (of three) started at Lafayette, we heard some complaints about shifting principals but on the whole, the intel was extremely positive. We looked seriously at private schools, and that remains an option for us financially. That said, we value the community much higher than other factors, so we stuck with Lafayette since it is much closer than the private alternatives. We made the right decision and it is not even close. Not only have the teachers been exceptional at Lafayette, but also all of our friends in private schools complain often about the lack of community. Most of the students at Lafayette live within a half a mile from the school. For us, that has meant extremely close ties, less driving, and more time developing relationships in our immediate community. For these reasons, we would rate our experience an 11 out of 10.

Overall Lafayette has been very good from an educational, social and communal standpoint. My only complaint is that they don't have an HCC program considering how many HCC eligible students they have. Fairmount is at capacity for their HCC program and students on the wait list have nowhere to go. I wish Lafayette could fill that void.
Great. I have two boys who have attended the school and have had great experiences. The teachers are very knowledgeable and caring and my boys have thrived.

schoolReviews.review: Madison just cancelled its honors classes from 2020-21 onward (same as all the other middle schools in Seattle.) HCC still exists for the few who can test into it, but everyone else will be stuck with dumbed down general ed.
9/10 on the disappointment scale. Yes, kids will be kids. However, the adults need to wake up and smell the coffee (and perhaps the blood in the water).

Madison has been a wonderful school so far. There are so many academic opportunities for the students. This is my daughter's first year in the district, but I have found that more advanced classes are available with testing. The music program is very good and I am really happy to say that it is completely free with borrowed instruments and music books. My daughter loves the after school programs provided at an additional cost through the YMCA. There are really cool programs such as Gaming, Coding, and Cooking. There is also free tutoring after school through the YMCA program. I found that the sports teams are also great. My daughter participated in the Soccer program this year. While it's run by parent volunteers, it's still a great opportunity for students. She's looking forward to the track team in the spring. I have found that the teachers are very thorough and well prepared. Grades are promptly reported on the online grading system. Whenever I have had questions regarding grades, the teachers were very prompt to respond. I've also found that the principal and counselor are also very helpful and genuinely care about making this a great school. The librarian is a true gem!!! She has Books and Bites at lunch time. She has a suggested reading list and whenever anyone reads all the books, she announces their names on the loud speaker. She really makes reading awesome! The school announces students of the day. They also have a monthly "Eat Lunch with Your Parent." It's really nice to be invited into the school to meet my daughter's friends and see what it's like during the school day. They also have a discipline program for students who are not being respectful. Overall, my daughter has found lots of friends since starting at this school. I've been pleasantly surprised since starting here!

We've loved our first two years at Madison. The teachers have been dedicated, focused and supportive. More than welcome to set up consultations whenever we needed some extra guidance. The school pulls from several great elementary schools- Lafayette, Schmitz park and Alki- and seems to get a really nice group of kids. The school community is broad enough that there's a niche for everyone- band kids, sports kids, etc... And as of 2015 it's now the middle school that the Fairmount park Spectrum and App program will feed to, so advanced learners can now stay in West Seattle.
We are so happy at Madison. Excellent teachers and supportive community. Madison has improved greatly in the last decade.
It is awesome there are awesome teachers there great they have good nice kids there the 6th graders are separated from the 7 and 8th grades go to this school it i sawesome
We are so happy at Madison. The overall caliber of teachers is outstanding. Madison is a great community and the school does an excellent job communicating with families.

schoolReviews.review: This school is a majority white school with terrible SpecialED support. The school also suffers with nonstop vaping, smoking, and drugs being done in the bathrooms with no apparent efforts to stop it from happening (I can't go to the bathroom due to how hazy it is in there and how strong the smell of vape is in the bathrooms, every one is like this). Besides that, I have been miserable due to the majority of classes using older, outdated "Chair tables" I'm unsure if that's the name or not. I would highly advise against attending this school, or having your child go here. I'd also like to say there are maybe 20 mixed race students in the school including myself.

I feel very included at this school. I am interested in most classes, and they are engaging. I've made many friends, and I like most of the teachers that have taught me. The counselors are wonderful, and I feel safe there. :)

This school was not a good experience for me. I didn’t feel welcome as a religious person, I’m a Muslim and pray 5 times a day and it was very hard praying at school .I also didn’t feel comfortable of this environment learning was very poor and stressing and there were a lot of drugs in the bathroom like I be seeing a group of people smoking in the bathroom, I’ve seen bullying and people not doing anything about it. I don’t like this school and I’m very much glad I’m not going to this school next year.

Outstanding. My closest relative graduated four years ago, to gain acceptance to Mount Holyoke then Columbia University. Her teachers were exceedingly supportive of her every endeavor, and if it were not for the stellar education at West Seattle High School, she never would have made it to the Ivy League and excelled there as well. The campus is like a small private college. Excellent sports, and activities like you would not find at other schools across the country.
Complete lack of resources, communication with parents, leadership, and subpar teaching staff.

Positive overall. The school is not great in every category, but I would say the school is great in many places that count, and with some effort can improve the areas that need it. It is important to say that the indicated rating the school has slightly lower than it should be based on a faulty state assessment reporting system. West Seattle High School has a program for students failing state assessments to retake them again the following year. The small fraction of students who do this do the testing at a different time of year than the general student population, and their test scores override and end up representing the overall pass rate for the entire school. As an example, the Biology Pass rate was actually closer to 80-85%, but because the students who failed the test the first time override the school’s score with their second-time test results, the report ends up indicate a 40-50% Pass rate.
My daughter was a student at WSHS and I pulled her out halfway through the year. The bullying problems at that school is out of control. I cannot recommend this school.

schoolReviews.review: Deciding to go to Pathfinder K-8 was one of the best choices I've made as a parent. We bought our house specifically so that we'd be in the attendance area for Fairmount Park and the geozone for Pathfinder, and every day I'm glad we did. Everyone at this school has chosen to come here, which means that the parent community is unmatched. The teachers are invested and highly engaged. No space does inclusivity perfectly, but we've personally had a great experience with accommodations and teamwork with admin. Our kids learn to be accepting of all kinds of abilities. The real clincher here is that the on-site before-and-after-school care "Blazing Trails" is the best run & most affordable school-age kid care in the city. We're lucky that West Seattle has so many good schools, and I'm sure they're all great, but in my opinion, this one is the best.

We have a 5th grader and Kindergartener at Pathfinder K-8 and are thrilled with the direction the school is going under the new(ish) leadership of Mrs Thomas and Ms Everman. The teachers have always been exceptional but they are happier and more engaged with the new administration. The admins send out regular surveys to families and then change policies based on responses to those surveys. The kids loop here - two years with the same teacher which creates stability and prevents the backslide at the start of the second year. The teachers already know them and group dynamics, and jump right back into learning. We have a very engaged PTSA and many programs unique to Pathfinder - camping every year for every grade level, a garden program, Share the Gift each Spring and many others. Parents are involved and there is a strong sense of community fostered by family volunteer opportunities such as the wreath making fundraiser and participation in classrooms and on fieldtrips. The learning and unique expeditionary curriculum puts Pathfinder on par with the local private schools. I toured them all and will be keeping my 5th grader at Pathfinder for middle school next year.

We love pathfinder . Our kids feel safe and nurtured. The teachers really care about their education and social emotional experience . The kids are all treated with respect and compassion . The new administration has really ensured a safe and healthy environment. As a parent I really appreciate strong PTSA community . We have made strong connections all in all .

Pathfinder K-8 is an absolutely exceptional project based learning school. As a choice school family we have felt incredibly lucky to have won the lottery and gotten a spot for our two kids. Our children attended both the elementary school and middle school during the past three years. Excellent teachers and highly engaged new school leadership. I recommend this school to anyone who wants their child to be known, cherished, and supported. Educational standards are excellent!

We’ve had a fantastic experience in the last 6 years at Pathfinder. My two kids have had EXCELLENT teaching throughout. Small class sizes, great outdoor ed. The school weathered a couple of difficult years with admin but has come back stronger than ever. Truly a gem of SPS.

I have been truly impressed with the transformation at Pathfinder over the past 18 months since the new administration took the helm. As a parent, it's heartening to witness such a positive shift in both the academic atmosphere and overall school culture. It feels like Pathfinder is truly living its mission of being inclusive, caring and a great place to learn through experiences designed for all ages. The dedication and vision of the new leadership team and the incredible staff they lead (we couldn't do it without this AMAZING staff) are evident in every corner of that building! They have prioritized not only strengthening core academic programs but also enriching students' educational experiences through the many offerings that happen at Pathfinder-- these initiatives are the center of the school community and what makes this place special. One of the standout programs is the school garden, which provides students with hands-on learning about sustainability, healthy living, caring for living things... It's wonderful to see the excitement in the student's eyes as they plant seeds and watch their efforts grow into harvest. Garden is not alone though. The music program (amazing teacher!), PE (such a fun time, our PE teacher is so creative-- and I love the new take on healthy movement she has taken), Art encouraging creativity and self-expression (last year's art showcase was so great, kids even got their pieces into the SAM)... and lastly, the library program which fosters a love for reading and learning along with the best librarian in the world!! Always refreshing the space, book collection and engaging with the kiddos in every way (including leading our ASB).The new administration has truly created an environment where students can thrive emotionally and academically. I am grateful for the positive impact these changes have had on my child and highly recommend Pathfinder to any family seeking a well-rounded and nurturing educational experience. And don't forget to get to know the staff. They are the soul behind everything that happens in this building.

As a parent at Pathfinder, I’ll admit things didn’t start perfectly due to past administrative challenges, but the transformation has been incredible since then with the new administration. The school feels supportive, engaged, and community driven. The teachers are outstanding, and the unique learning experiences like frequent field trips and annual camping make it truly special. I also love the K-8 model, which helps kids navigate the middle school years better.

schoolReviews.review: My daughter has had a very positive experience. She has built a strong foundation in core academic areas, and has also learned about art, gardening, forestry, and so many other areas of interest. Strong communication from teachers, principal and PTA. Lots of opportunities for families to get involved.

This school has new leadership, and we've had a great experience. As an option school, most families are involved and interested in their child's education. It's helped round out the school with the after-school enrichment and other opportunities outside of just core academics that we've seen a number of families put time and effort into. If anything we wish SPS would fund these schools, and all their schools better. As our kids have gotten older we've seen benefits to the project-based work they do, and appreciate the number of long-time teachers.

I think people frequently over exaggerate how bad this school is. i mean, of couse they do. people rarelt like their own schools, because people rarely like learning. ive been at this chool 9/10 of the years its been in operation. ive never been to another school, so im not sure houw accurate this will be. i dont think this school is great but i would not say this school is horrible. some of the eachers are less than ideal, but still do a pretty good job of teaching. the principal and vice principal is where a significant problem arises. they do not know how to deal with conflict, or how to treat all studens equally. the students are mostly fine. i cant give a review on them because your treatment by students really varries on who you are, what grade youre in, and what year youre going to this school.
Pulled child out after one year because she seemed depressed here. Currently thriving at a different school.
1/10, only thing good was one teacher for one year that got fired despite being most effective teacher I had ever had
I would highly recommend STEM K-8. It has been a great experience for our son over the last seven years (he has been there since it opened in 2012).

I wouldn’t recommend anyone with a motive to succeed to go to this school. I found my time there the worst experiences I’ve ever had. Probably due to the principal’s unfathomable way of dealing with issues, or the lack thereof.

schoolReviews.review: As both an alumna and current parent, Holy Rosary has been such a meaningful part of our family’s life. The school offers a strong academic foundation while creating a truly supportive, values-driven community where students and families feel known and cared for. We’ve especially appreciated the dedicated teachers, welcoming environment, and the lasting friendships and sense of belonging the school fosters.

We feel very thankful to be part of the HRS community over the past 6 years. The supportive environment enables my daughter to thrive socially, emotionally and academically. We’re grateful for the teachers and staff at HRS and will miss being an active part of the school.

HRS has been a wonderful community for our whole family, especially our eldest who is graduating after nine years there. We feel fortunate to be a part of the gator crew and feel the love from the amazing staff.

Holy Rosary School has been a wonderful experience for our family. What initially drew us to the school was the strong sense of community and the shared commitment from educators and families toward raising confident, well-rounded children, and the school truly lived up to those expectations.The academics are strong, but we especially appreciated the emphasis on communication and presentation skills, faith formation, and community giving. Students are encouraged to grow not only academically, but also as thoughtful leaders and kind people.One thing that makes Holy Rosary special is how welcoming and connected the community is. New families are paired with ambassador families to help them navigate the school and activities, and the buddy program pairs older students with younger students to help foster leadership and connection across grades.Families should know that parent involvement and volunteering are an important part of the culture, which helps create the strong community feel the school is known for.As our son graduates 8th grade, we feel he is well prepared for high school and excited for the transition ahead.

This was the right choice for our student at the right time. He started at HRS in the 7th grade; he needed an academic challenge. HRS was a good match for academic focus, community, and friends. The teachers are very open to conversations, and the parent group is very welcoming. We've appreciated our time at HRS, and our kiddo is looking forward to high school. It is a good feeling; he's ready, and we know he is academically prepared to do well.
We've had a really positive experience at Holy rosary. We feel that the school's operations during COVID in particular were exceptional. We also like that the school cares about diversity.

If you are looking for a wonderful K-8 learning experience for your child, you will absolutely find it at Holy Rosary. We have two students at HRS and could not be more grateful for this special community. The warmth, kindness, and genuine care from the faculty and staff is evident. Our children have grown not only in academic knowledge but in faith, service, confidence, and character. The teachers and staff are exceptional—deeply dedicated, nurturing, and attentive to the individual needs of every student. You won't find a more dedicated group of people - many have been teaching at HRS for 20+ years! We wholeheartedly recommend HRS.

Hope always says they are the small school with a big hug and I have always felt that with our Son. He started in pre-kay at Hope and had one year at a public elementary school and we pulled him out and brought him back to Hope. He is now just finishing 8th grade. It was the best decision we have ever made to help our son realize his full potential for both personal and academic growth. The new north campus is awesome and a huge win for the hope facilities. Our son loves the new space. He has received a very strong preparation with a specific focus in Math and other core subjects. He got into a very selective high school based on the work he has done including doing well in all of his placement tests etc. He has developed very strong relationships with the other kids and the fantastic teachers. Hope has been an incredible experience for him.

My daughter started here in 6th grade this year and we are thrilled to be a part of the Hope community. The level of professionalism, kindness, sincerity, humility and overall community feel is incredibly high. Having been part of a close knit community in the Seattle Public School district, we were worried that we would not find that in the private school sector. Boy were we wrong. The greatness of this school starts from the top with Mrs.O who knows all the kids by name and is out there every day meeting with the parents and students. Seattle Public School had gone in a direction that we didn’t trust for our daughter. The agenda they pushed became a higher priority than academics. There was so much confusion and uncertainty. Switching to Hope has been extremely challenging academically for us (which Mrs.O told us we would see) but I wouldn’t trade it for the world. I absolutely love watching (and helping) my daughter learn study habits, understanding the importance of routine & hard work, making new friends amidst the hardships of puberty, and so much more. It has truly been a rich and rewarding experience for us. I love that the faith they teach aligns with our beliefs but I also love that the Hope community is full of other faiths and beliefs that are all welcome there. I cannot express just how grateful we are to have joined this amazing group of students, staff and parents.

We moved my son to Hope Lutheran after he suffered through a year of online learning during the pandemic. He was not in a good state. Being isolated was highly stressful for him. I was worried about him. His best friend had moved to Hope. I knew from him that his their grade's class was not full to capacity and he would probably get more teacher attention (there is 1 class per grade).After 3 years, it's not only like the pandemic experience never happened -- he is doing better than before the pandemic. I am SO happy we took a chance on this private school. We had not budgeted for such a move, but the value for the money is outstanding.The student-teacher ratio is something you will never get at public school. My son is seen, heard, known, and loved. I personally care about that more than academics, but their academics are excellent as well. Most of the teachers seem to have master's degrees as well as tons of experience. They radiate joy, warmth, purpose, and sincerity. There are no burnouts here.On the last day of 5th grade, may son was about to get in my car but went back and told his teacher Ms. Robertson, "You're the nicest teacher I have ever had!" I think I shed a tear.I am a big believer in small schools. Whatever opportunities may be missed are more than made up for in the environment of increased adult contact and friendship that is made possible. That is what I am paying for and it is well worth it.I know non-religious families may hesitate to place their child in a religious school. We are not a religious family and most of the families there aren't religious. They have a class called Faith and they have chapel once a week. They learn about other religions too. I believe this rounds out his education wonderfully and gives him an enhanced perspective on the world, and on history.Middle School: They have just purchased and remodeled the old Seattle Lutheran High School building, and middle school will move there starting the 2024-2025 school year. This is a fantastic opportunity to place your child in an excellent facility with all the same benefits of the small school environment. I only wish Hope offered high school as well!

I do not recommend this school at all. The teachers are always right and the students' opinion is never valid. Even if you voice your opinion, the school will not allow you to continue there. The teachers and principle continue to make favourites, they allow them to call down to the office any time that they like, pull them out of class for no real reason, and let them do things with younger grades. If you are a child of colour then you are automatically considered a problem child. This school is focused on faith(Which is not a bad thing), but they do not consider that not everything has to revolve around it and don't consider that the lives of the children matter more. The teachers don't own up to their own actions, they say the opposite thing that they originally said before, then making it the child's fault. The school wastes money, they have so many fundraisers but spends it on painting a lion in the gym. The teachers are forced to work really late; they stay way after hours to finish their lesson plans.

After a tumultuous 1.5 pandemic years, my boys needed some solid, in-person, truth-filled learning. And they got it at Hope. Though many of the kids have been there since pre-K, my 6th and 8th graders were welcomed. The gaps left by virtual learning were quickly filled and, with the help of gifted and caring teachers, they both realized they were better at math than they previously thought. My youngest has a visual disability (though he's so capable most people wouldn't know) and the Hope admin did whatever they could to ensure he'd thrive- which he did. Very bummed that my 8th grader only got one year there, but my 6th grader doesn't want to be anywhere else for Middle School.

My child has attended the preschool program and is now finishing his elementary year here before middle school. We enjoy this school, my son likes attending here and has excelled in many areas, math, spelling, learning cursive while also having lots of creative learning time. The school has involved season sports programs and clubs. The staff at the school are friendly and show a lot of care for the kids and the school community. The school staff were there for families during challenging times and during covid. The classrooms accommodated families in the best ways they could, for example the classroom would allow you to attend either online or in person during the covid year. I do not know any other elementary school that offered this. Most of the students were safely able to attend during the year while many schools went fully remote. They truly go above and beyond for the kids. Children receive quality academics and spiritual support for their development which was helpful for my child's well being during difficult times in the world. He has had amazing teachers here each year while at this school. The staff and the principal due a wonderful job here, are quick to answer any questions and assist. They greet the children in the morning daily outside of the school too! The kinda charm you just don't get in the city nowadays. The school offers small class sizes which works well for my child who can get pretty side tracked in larger learning settings. The classrooms offer flexibility to accommodate various learning abilities. Each year starting in preschool they have the children speak, perform and participate in front of a large school group during chapel for events as a class which develops confidence and public speaking skills early on. This is something I never developed or participated in at school, not having experience until college years so my anxiety with public speaking was pretty severe. They do a nice job encouraging the children. The classroom also facilitates independence of the students as they get older, being responsible for yourself and your own work, taking accountability, communicating, self planning your to dos, developing self confidence while feeling good about asking questions or getting extra help when needed. The kids have fun too, even in fifth grade they are not too old to bring a stuffy on Friday, have game time, ect. The school offers family engagement and encourages volunteering.

What a wonderful community of supportive and caring teachers and staff. During a year full of uncertainty for families and children (COVID), this community was resilient, reliable, and provided something we could rely on for stability and support. We've become friends with the families in our son's class and have been able to organize play dates (outdoors) outside of the classroom. We feel so blessed to be part of Hope.

This has been a fantastic experience for my son. He is a Freshman. The school is small but very inviting. He is working ahead in math and the administration has been eager to place him in the more senior classes. He participates in sports and robotics. We love the teachers and coaches.

We have had a wonderful experience at Seattle Lutheran. It's small size really allows kids to gain confidence and participate in everything the school has to offer. We are not a religious family, but appreciate the message of grace. The religion class is a little less intellectual than I had hoped, but still a good introduction to different beliefs.

As a parent with two students enrolled at SLHS, I highly recommend. Teachers are interested in each student individually. Classics are taught. All students are accepted and loved for who they are. Awesome art, robotics, drama and athletic programs are offered.
Not worth the financial investment. Unfortunate leadership attitude and focus

Do your research. We have a good student without high expectations for academics. We looked for the whole experience (academic, character growth, social group, sports, electives, and culture respect). SeaLu is disappointing. Academics are average to below-average. Men and women in leadership make strong judgements against student open conversations of religion, gender and race diversity, and alternative viewpoints. The number of students needing severe disciplinary action raised concern as did the mean spirited in-person and social media badgering to the kids who did not come from the Hope Lutheran feeder school. The parent association is run year after year by the same group who are uninviting, run the same activities without opportunities for new parents, and openly gossip about families. We tried very hard to roll with the frustrations, but found that

I have a child that is a Junior at Seattle Lutheran High School. We are not Lutheran and she has two moms, but we have found the administration and teachers overwhelmingly welcoming and supportive. Our daughter loves it so much there. The teachers are amazing and so helpful to her. She has formed strong bonds with the teachers and all the other students. The school size allows her to know the entire student body and be involved in any extra-curricular activity she is interested in. When the pandemic started, they switched to online learning within a week. I recommend this school to everyone.

As a former teacher, I have the highest respect for the other educators who work here, but the administrator is dragging the school down. He is unorganized, sexist, controlling, and unwilling to accept criticism of his actions and decisions.On a whole, there is a tendency in the administration to cater to the concerns of a small number of parents who give money or have connections while ignoring the wishes of the bulk of parents, the needs of their faculty, and--often--research into best practices. This school could be so good. The teachers there care about their students and want to challenge them to reach their full potential, but they are hampered by the administrations ineptitude.
